target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer: one half/side of the part + lanceolate PATO_0001877)
reason: Describes one half of an unequal-sided leaf or pinna (the acroscopic or upper side) as lanceolate; the quality is lanceolate, the bearer is the half.

target: tendril absent (no generic PO class: union of PO_0025361 leaf tendril, PO_0025362 leaflet tendril, PO_0025363 leaf apex tendril, PO_0025364 branch tendril, PO_0025365 stem apex tendril, PO_0025366 leaf rachis tendril, PO_0025367 prophyll tendril) absent
reason: Without tendrils = complement of has_part some tendril; PO has only the specific tendril classes, so the absence is of their union.
Three-flowered inflorescences or cymes are a count of flowers, like 'few-flowered'.
Saucer-like disk, hypanthium = round and shallowly concave: the existing FLOPO saucer-shaped.
Two-leaved pseudobulbs are a leaf count; where it means two leaflets (bifoliolate) the counted part is the leaflet.
The quality is ridged; 'finely' is a degree modifier. The French 'finement ridée' (finely wrinkled) belongs to rugose PATO_0001359.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: Comparative ('plus fin', 'shorter, finer') without the part it is compared with, like 'narrower'.

PATO calcified is defined as encrusted or impregnated with calcium carbonate, the usual case ('incrusted with calcium carbonate'). The French midrib 'incrustée' means sunken (PATO_0002416) and needs that reading.
Analogy to a mango fixes no defined shape (size, outline and compression all vary); too vague for a term and rare.
Not sticky = not adhering to what touches it: PATO non-adhesive, the opposite of adhesive PATO_0002331.
Pinched in the lower half = narrowed as if squeezed: constricted. 'Laterally pinched' lemmas are laterally compressed (PATO_0002054).
A tactile impression (of mucilaginous inner bark or a slimy plant) with no defined morphological quality; rare.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: ovate PATO_0001891 [ovoid] - elliptic PATO_0000947 [ellipsoid])
reason: A compound of two existing shape values with a degree modifier; no term needed.
Antler-like spines and appendages are repeatedly forked ('up to twice forked'); the shared quality is branched.
Perceptible veins, ribs = visible, as rule C323 'evident'; 'barely/hardly perceptible' reads as inconspicuous PATO_0000464.
Fronds or sori shortly spaced = set close together, the opposite of FLOPO:0991189 distant, which the previous review set against crowded.
Nearly but not perfectly spherical: PATO subspherical.

label: lithophytic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing on rock, attached to the rock surface or rooted in its crevices.
reason: A habit position like FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic, 0991111 terrestrial, 0991112 aquatic; the rock is not a plant part, so the relational PATO attached to does not fit. NOTE: probably outside PATO's scope (where an organism lives).
Very large, as 'enlarged' (rule C180) and 'tall' (C183).
A false raceme is an inflorescence resembling a raceme but not one: the existing FLOPO raceme-like.

label: hemiepiphytic
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its growing as an epiphyte for only part of its life, either starting on a host and later rooting in the ground or starting in the ground and later losing its connection to it.
reason: A distinct, well-defined habit; sibling of FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic, which it would wrongly overstate. NOTE: probably outside PATO's scope.
Forming tubers = bearing tubers; PO_0025522 covers shoot axis and root tubers.
Primary veins radiating from one point at the leaf base: PATO actinodromous.
One source sentence ('ovary with a pileiform cap'); cap-shaped fixes no single shape (hemispherical or conical), and the bearer is the cap, not the ovary.
Woolly with wavy hairs: the covering is lanate; the wavy form is a quality of the hairs, not a new value.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: As 'shorter' (C247); with 'than X' it is handled by docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md.
Partly sheathing = at least partially enclosing the axis: PATO clasping; full sheathing is FLOPO:0991105.
A vague abundance of branches, seed or roots with no defined quality.

label: aphyllopodic
definition: A structural quality inhering in a culm or fertile shoot by virtue of its lowest leaves being bladeless sheaths or having much reduced blades, the shoot usually arising laterally from beneath the leaves of a previous shoot.
reason: A frequent sedge term (150 statements) with no PATO or FLOPO term; the 'lowest leaves only' constraint is too awkward to write as a lamina-absent rule on every use. Opposite of phyllopodic.

label: phyllopodic
definition: A structural quality inhering in a culm or fertile shoot by virtue of its lowest leaves bearing well-developed blades, the shoot arising from the centre of a leaf tuft.
reason: The sedge counterpart of aphyllopodic (137 statements), distinct from FLOPO:0991012 leafy, which concerns foliage along the whole axis.
